instruction: Visit https://www.w3.org/standards/ and create a document called "web_standards.docx" on the desktop. List at least 3 web standards or technologies mentioned on the page using a bulleted list format.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires visiting a website, creating a docx document, and formatting content as a bulleted list with at least 3 items. Evaluator checks if the document contains at least 3 bullet points.

llm_judge_reasons: Content verification IMPLEMENTED: Metric checks bullet texts for web standards keywords (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, XML, WCAG, WAI-ARIA, etc.) - comprehensive list of 48+ keywords from W3C standards
Format verification works correctly: Getter properly detects bullet points via LibreOffice paragraph styles (List/Bullet styles), metric correctly checks min_bullets >= 3
Semantic coverage is strong: Evaluator verifies both structure (bulleted list format) and content (web standards/technologies keywords)
Parameter handling is correct: Metric correctly accesses expected.get('requires_bullets') and expected.get('min_bullets') directly (expected IS the rules dict when type='rule')
Postconfig is appropriate: Activates LibreOffice window and saves file (Ctrl+S) before evaluation to ensure document state is persisted

Minor limitation: Cannot verify that user actually visited https://www.w3.org/standards/ URL (no Chrome history check), but keyword matching provides reasonable confidence that content is from a web standards source
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional enhancement: Add Chrome history verification to confirm https://www.w3.org/standards/ was visited, though keyword matching already provides strong content validation
Optional enhancement: Could add partial credit scoring (e.g., 0.5 if has bullets but no web standards keywords, 1.0 if both)
